title: Compatible polynomial-local regular presentations over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A,B$ be commutative local $k$-algebras essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], and let $f:A\to B$ be a local $k$-algebra homomorphism, meaning $f(\mathfrak m_A)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$. There exist regular local $k$-algebras $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme], both essentially of finite type over $k$, surjective local $k$-algebra maps $q:R\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $v:S\twoheadrightarrow B$, and a flat local $k$-algebra map $u:R\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] such that $vu=fq$. Moreover, $F=S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is a regular local $k$-algebra essentially of finite type over $k$. No flatness of $f$, completeness of $A,B$, or separability of their residue fields is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00QM (definition-essentially-finite-p-t), localization of a finite type algebra, and Tag 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring), polynomial regularity. Agent-formulated simultaneous polynomial-local presentation: take R a localized finite polynomial algebra surjecting onto A and S a localization of R[Y_1,...,Y_m] surjecting onto B; the closed fibre is a localized polynomial algebra over the residue field of R.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] and [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], choose a finite type $k$-algebra $C$, a multiplicative subset $W$, an identification $A=W^{-1}C$, and generators $c_1,\ldots,c_n$ of $C$. Let $P=k[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ and let $a:P\to A$ send $X_i$ to $c_i/1$, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Every element of $A$ is $a(h)/a(t)$ for some $h,t\in P$ with $a(t)$ a unit: lift the numerator in $C$ and its denominator in $W$ along the polynomial surjection. Put $\mathfrak p=a^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)$ and $R=P_{\mathfrak p}$. For $t\notin\mathfrak p$, $a(t)$ is a unit in the local ring $A$, so $q(h/t)=a(h)a(t)^{-1}$ is well defined by the fraction relation of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. It is surjective by the preceding fraction description. Its inverse image of $\mathfrak m_A$ is exactly $\mathfrak pR=\mathfrak m_R$, because its denominators are units. Thus $q$ is local.

source.place: Tag 00QM (definition-essentially-finite-p-t), Tag 00F3 (definition-finite-type), and Tag 00CO (definition-localization); direct fraction construction.

proof.text: Apply the same finite type and localization definitions to $B$: choose a finite type $k$-algebra $C'$, denominators $W'$, and generators $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ of $C'$, regarded as elements of $B$. Put $D=P[Y_1,\ldots,Y_m]=k[X,Y]$, and define $b:D\to B$ by $X_i\mapsto f(a(X_i))$ and $Y_j\mapsto b_j$, using polynomial evaluation [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Set $Q=b^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)$ and $S=D_Q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The formula $v(h/t)=b(h)b(t)^{-1}$ defines a local map $S\to B$: $t\notin Q$ has unit image, and $v^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=QS$. Every element of $B$ is a fraction of polynomials in the $b_j$ with denominator from $W'$, so this formula is surjective even without the $X$ variables.

Locality of $f$ implies $f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$: it gives one inclusion, and an element outside $\mathfrak m_A$ is a unit, whose image remains a unit. Consequently $Q\cap P=\mathfrak p$. Hence inclusion $P\hookrightarrow D$ induces $u:R\to S$, $h/t\mapsto h/t$. The maximal ideals are $\mathfrak pR$ and $QS$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; the equality of contractions proves that $u$ is local. On every fraction $h/t\in R$, both $vu$ and $fq$ have value $f(a(h))f(a(t))^{-1}$, proving $vu=fq$. All maps fix $k$ by their formulas.

source.place: Tag 00CO (definition-localization), universal fraction formulas; locality of the given homomorphism.

proof.text: The rings $R=P_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S=D_Q$ are regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], applied to the $n$ and $n+m$ variable polynomial rings over $k$. They are essentially of finite type over $k$ by [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], since $P$ and $D$ are finite type polynomial algebras.

source.place: Tag 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring), regularity of every prime localization; Tag 00QM.

proof.text: Put $E=R[Y_1,\ldots,Y_m]$. It is the localization of $D$ at $U=P\setminus\mathfrak p$: a polynomial in $Y$ with finitely many fractional coefficients is written with one common denominator in $U$, and equality is detected after multiplying by a further element of $U$. Since $U\cap Q=\varnothing$, let $Q_E$ be the inverse image of $QS$ in $E$. The formulas $E\to S$, $h/t\mapsto h/t$, and $D_Q\to E_{Q_E}$, $h/s\mapsto(h/1)/(s/1)$, identify $S=E_{Q_E}$: for $h/t\in E$, membership in $Q_E$ is $h\in Q$, so the displayed maps invert precisely the required denominators and their composites fix all fractions. These are the fraction constructions in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 00CO (definition-localization), iterated localization; explicit common-denominator and inverse formulas.

proof.text: The monomial expansion in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] identifies $E$ with the free $R$-module on the monomials in $Y$. Thus $R\to E$ is flat by the free-module clause of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. The map $E\to E_{Q_E}=S$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. Their composite is the map $u$ already constructed, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp] proves that $u$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 051G (lemma-local-artinian-characterize-flat), proof opening sentence on free/projective flatness; Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), (1); Tag 00HC (lemma-composition-flat).

proof.text:
Let $K=R/\mathfrak m_R=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, a field by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The coefficient-reduction map $E\to K[Y]$ is surjective and has kernel $\mathfrak m_RE$: reduce each of the finitely many coefficients, and a polynomial reduces to zero exactly when all its coefficients lie in $\mathfrak m_R$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Locality of $u$ gives $\mathfrak m_RE\subset Q_E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] to $E$, this ideal, and $Q_E$. Writing $\overline Q_E=Q_E/\mathfrak m_RE$, it gives
$$F=S/\mathfrak m_RS\cong K[Y]_{\overline Q_E}.$$
Here $\overline Q_E$ is prime and proper because $Q_E$ is. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], now over the possibly inseparable field extension $K/k$, proves that $F$ is regular local.

Finally $\mathfrak m_RS=\mathfrak pS$, since $\mathfrak m_R=\mathfrak pR$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] also to $D$, the ideal $\mathfrak pD\subset Q$, and $Q$: it identifies $F$ with $(D/\mathfrak pD)_{Q/\mathfrak pD}$. The $k$-algebra $D/\mathfrak pD$ is finite type, generated by the residue classes of the finitely many $X_i,Y_j$, by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Consequently its localization $F$ is essentially of finite type over $k$ by [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. This verifies the last required clause without requiring finite generation of $K$ as a $k$-algebra.
